title: Epochal hedge and throttle for live edge failover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: For hosted API traffic we must support active-active edge gateways across regions while preserving availability and stream continuity for long-lived streaming sessions. Current behavior during a regional ejection or capacity degradation: abrupt traffic shift -> connection resets for streaming callers -> significant request retry amplification and SLO violations (p99 latency + error spikes).

Goal: Implement an epochal (stage-wise) hedging + throttle mechanism that enables traffic draining from a degraded region while a remote region ramps up, minimizing live streaming interruption and avoiding overload cascades. The feature combines (1) controlled traffic gradient shifts, (2) short-lived hedging requests to remote region(s), (3) per-session lightweight checkpoint/resume tokens, and (4) SLO-aware circuit breakers and load-shedding. This ticket covers design, runtime changes, rollout, dashboards, canary plan, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Edge gateway can shift traffic from region A to region B in staged epochs (0-5) with configurable epoch duration and percent increments
Long-lived streaming sessions see <1% forced disconnects attributable to mid-shift failover in canary traffic (internal test) and <3% in production rollout
No upstream region exceeds 85% util during sweep; automatic back-off occurs when SLO headroom <5%
Circuit breakers trigger per-shard and per-customer with exponential backoff and are observable in console dashboards
Automated rollback and safe-fallback to dual-write hedging within 60s if error amplification detected
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit + integration tests for epoch scheduler, hedging client, and resume token format — target: staging runtime-1.22
Phase 1 (canary): 1% of traffic (non-critical orgs) for 48h, monitor p50/p90/p99 latency, connection reset rate, and kernel saturation
Phase 2 (regional): 10% of traffic in a single region with conservative epoch increments (5% per epoch, 60s epochs), runbook on standby
Phase 3 (global ramp): 50% then 100% with auto-throttle enabled and telemetry gating
Post-rollout: 30d reliability burn-in with regression checks and retrospectives
telemetry_and_alerts: New dashboards: epoch_progress, hedged_request_ratio, resume_success_rate, per-shard_utilization
SLO alarms: p99 latency > 2x historical baseline for 5m triggers pager and auto-rollback
Safety gates: downstream_utilization > 85% -> throttle increase pauses and reduces epoch step size
implementation_notes: Epoch scheduler: implement as a lightweight coordinator in the gateway control plane with idempotent epoch state stored in regional config-store (TTL 120s)
Hedging strategy: for live streaming handoffs send short-lived hedged warmup requests (0.5s soft timeout) to candidate regions to pre-populate KV caches and warm kernels
Resume tokens: compact opaque token (region, epoch, stream-shard, offset) signed with KMS key; token must be single-key-stable across minor runtime restarts
Circuit breakers: per-shard leaky-bucket counters with SLO headroom input; breakers expose reason codes (cpu_shed, kv_miss_surge, net_err) for diagnostics
Load-shedding policy: graceful reject with 429 + Retry-After for non-streaming requests; for streams return resume_token in final event so clients can reconnect once epoch completes
Backward compatibility: default behavior off; opt-in via account flag; new clients should tolerate resume_token in disconnect event
Testing: create synthetic stream harness that simulates N=10k long-lived sessions with random prompt lengths and reconnection backoff to validate amplification bounds
